pr.body:
<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

Remove reference to DuckDB

**Why do we need this feature?**

See the blog post describing the vulnerability, for which a fix was rolled out to all Grafana versions earlier today:
https://grafana.com/blog/2024/10/17/grafana-security-release-critical-severity-fix-for-cve-2024-9264/

The full extent of our documentation around this feature seems to be here:
https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/81666/files#diff-16fb71b28e5b6197615abba8a07bc73d9bf75ebc60311663e1c29976de5cc9a6

All we've documented is that the feature-flag exists. That flag still exists in the codebase, so I'm tempted not to touch that documentation for now. We can always follow up with more improvements after this PR.

**Who is this feature for?**

Everyone

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

This moves the security fix into Grafana repo itself, now that it has been publicly announced. We need this here so we can clean up and simplify our Security-releases pipeline once again.

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
   Behaviour of this patch was already verified manually by @toddtreece. See his confirmation of this on our private slack, [here](https://raintank-corp.slack.com/archives/C07P60RBAUD/p1727902629844259?thread_ts=1727901896.911799&cid=C07P60RBAUD)
   Tested again on the Ephemeral instance here: https://ephemeral1511182194942samjewe.grafana-dev.net/d/be18gem24w2dcf/test-sql-expressions-bugfix?from=now-1h&to=now&timezone=browser
- [ ] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc.
pr.title: ServerSideExpressions: Disable SQL Expressions to prevent RCE and LFI vulnerability

raw_findings.body: Users can create or retain SQL expressions in the UI, but every such query fails at backend parsing despite the feature appearing available.
raw_findings.evidence: return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")
raw_findings.failure_mode: Client and server capabilities diverge, producing user-visible query failures for a feature the UI says is enabled.
raw_findings.impact: Users can create or retain SQL expressions in the UI, but every such query fails at backend parsing despite the feature appearing available.
raw_findings.root_cause: The backend was changed to unconditionally reject SQL expressions without changing the existing frontend feature-toggle path that advertises them.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Disable or remove the SQL expression option from the frontend capability data when this server-side kill switch is active, or make the feature toggle consistently report SQL as unavailable.
raw_findings.title: SQL remains visible in the frontend while the backend rejects it
raw_findings.trigger: An installation has the existing sqlExpressions feature toggle enabled, causing the frontend to offer SQL expressions, and a query is parsed through the new expression parser.

raw_findings.body: The documentation promises SQL and DuckDB expression support, but the backend returns an implementation error for every SQL expression.
raw_findings.evidence: return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")
raw_findings.failure_mode: Operators make configuration decisions based on stale capability documentation and encounter guaranteed query failures.
raw_findings.impact: The documentation promises SQL and DuckDB expression support, but the backend returns an implementation error for every SQL expression.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch changes the runtime contract of sqlExpressions but leaves the existing feature-toggle description unchanged.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the sqlExpressions feature-toggle documentation to state that the feature is disabled, or remove the toggle and its documentation until an implementation is restored.
raw_findings.title: Feature-toggle documentation still claims disabled SQL support is available
raw_findings.trigger: An administrator follows the documented sqlExpressions toggle description and enables it after this patch.

raw_findings.body: The identifier falsely suggests that the parser still uses DuckDB, which can mislead maintenance and security review about whether untrusted SQL is being executed by the removed engine.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Code review and future maintenance receive an inaccurate description of the active SQL backend.
raw_findings.impact: The identifier falsely suggests that the parser still uses DuckDB, which can mislead maintenance and security review about whether untrusted SQL is being executed by the removed engine.
raw_findings.root_cause: The dependency construction was replaced without updating the engine-specific local variable name.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the variable to db, or remove this dead parser path entirely if SQL support is intentionally disabled.
raw_findings.title: Parser retains a misleading DuckDB identifier after removing DuckDB
raw_findings.trigger: A maintainer investigates or changes the SQL parser after the DuckDB dependency and implementation have been removed.

raw_findings.body: A regression that reintroduces SQL execution, or an inconsistent legacy-parser bypass, can merge without a test proving that SQL expressions remain rejected after the security fix.
raw_findings.evidence: return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")
raw_findings.failure_mode: The security behavior depends on untested control flow and can silently regress during later parser or feature-toggle changes.
raw_findings.impact: A regression that reintroduces SQL execution, or an inconsistent legacy-parser bypass, can merge without a test proving that SQL expressions remain rejected after the security fix.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch replaces the SQL implementation with a security kill switch but adds no regression coverage for the two backend parsing paths.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add tests covering SQL input with the new expression parser enabled and disabled, plus the legacy buildCMDNode path, asserting that SQL commands are rejected and no query execution occurs.
raw_findings.title: No regression test verifies that both SQL parsing paths stay disabled
raw_findings.trigger: A future change enables the expression parser or modifies the SQL feature-toggle handling without manually exercising SQL queries.
